_comment: Visual-QA priors library (ADR 0057). Each prior describes a common-sense world fact + which visual assertion to emit when it applies to the entities present in a given game. yume-visual-tester walks each level's entities, matches them against each prior's trigger, and emits a concrete test instance into visual_test_plan.json. Priors are content (JSON), not engine code — extensible by any author + reviewed by the team. New priors should be added here whenever a post-mortem reveals a generalizable visual rule.

_schema.description: one-line explanation of the world fact
_schema.trigger: what entity shapes does this prior apply to. Mirrors engine query language (tags_any, tags_all, tags_none, def_id). For two-entity priors, use entities_a + entities_b. For single-entity, use entity. For unconditional (always emit one test), omit trigger.

emit.params: concrete param values; supports tokens <a.id>, <a.def>, <b.id>, <entity.id>, etc. that the skill resolves to actual entity ids at plan-emit time

_schema.priority: high | medium | low. high = always emit. medium = emit if not over plan budget. low = emit only when explicitly requested.
_schema.max_pairs: for two-entity priors, cap how many pairs to test (default 3, so 100 trees don't blow up the plan)

priors.description: Trees are taller than human-sized characters. Catches scale_init mismatch where a tree was authored at the wrong state.scale.
Buildings, shelters, huts are taller than human-sized characters.
Rabbits, mice, prey-type small animals are shorter than human-sized characters.
Buildings and large props rest on the ground (no visible gap under base, no clipping below ground plane).
Rigged animated characters use foot-pivot (state.position is ground contact point, not geometric center). Catches stale y_offset from a static-era mesh.

When the GDD aesthetic includes Fellowship, every pair of named NPCs must be visually distinguishable at a glance (different mesh, palette, or scale). Without this the player can't tell characters apart.
Wide-angle sanity sweep from each corner to catch mystery cubes (logical entities authored without visual.hidden). Always emitted regardless of level contents.
When the semantic biome map has a water region, the water surface should show specular response (low roughness + slight metallic).
Grass biome should be matte (high roughness, no specular).
NPCs explicitly associated with a focal anchor (fire_pit, well, shrine) via schedule or proximity tag should face that anchor during their default state.

Entities whose def files appear in the session's git diff get prioritized audits. The skill prepends these tests to the plan and runs them first so regressions to recently-changed defs are caught immediately. Operates at plan-generation time — the trigger reads git diff state, not entity tags.
